lesson.title: Base times height
lesson.body: The area of a parallelogram is base × height. The height is the straight-up distance between the base and the opposite side, at a right angle to the base: not the slanted side.

lesson.title: A triangle is half
lesson.body: Two copies of a triangle make a parallelogram, so a triangle's area is base × height ÷ 2.

lesson.title: The trapezoid formula
lesson.body: A trapezoid has two parallel sides. Its area is (the two parallel sides added) × height ÷ 2: the average width times the height.

lesson.title: Why it works
lesson.body: Two copies of a trapezoid, one turned over, make a parallelogram whose base is the two parallel sides together.

lesson.title: A square metre
lesson.body: 1 m = 100 cm, so a square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm: 1 m² = 10000 cm², not 100 cm².

lesson.title: Work in one unit
lesson.body: Before you multiply or divide lengths, make sure they are in the same unit: metres with metres, centimetres with centimetres.

lesson.title: Split or take away
lesson.body: Break a figure into rectangles and triangles and add their areas, or take a cut-away part from a bigger rectangle.

lesson.title: Perimeter is the way around
lesson.body: Area counts square units inside; perimeter adds the lengths around the edge. Cutting a corner from a rectangle keeps the same perimeter.

templates.construct: Find the area of a parallelogram, telling the height from the slanted side

formats.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of {b} cm, slanted sides of {s} cm and a height of {h} cm. What is its area?
A piece of card is cut as a parallelogram with a base of {b} cm, slanted sides of {s} cm and a height of {h} cm. What is its area?

hints: Area of a parallelogram = base × height.
The height is the straight-up distance, {h} cm, not the slanted side.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² uses the slanted side. The height meets the base at a right angle: {h} cm.
{value} cm is the distance around. Area is base × height.
{value} cm² halves it, as for a triangle. A parallelogram is base × height.

templates.construct: Find the area of a triangle

formats.prompt: A triangle has a base of {b} cm, a height of {h} cm and a slanted side of {s} cm. What is its area?
A triangular flag is {b} cm along the bottom and {h} cm high. What is its area?

hints: Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2.
templates.explain: A triangle is half a parallelogram: {b} × {h} ÷ 2 = {answer} cm².

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² is base × height. A triangle is half of that.
{value} cm² uses a side as the height. The height is {h} cm, at a right angle to the base.

templates.construct: Find the height of a triangle from its area and base

formats.prompt: A triangle has an area of {A} cm² and a base of {b} cm. What is its height?
A triangular flag has an area of {A} cm² and a base of {b} cm. What is its height?

hints: Area = base × height ÷ 2, so base × height = 2 × area.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm is {A} ÷ {b}. The area is half of base × height, so double {A} first.
{value} cm is {A} − {b}. Undo base × height ÷ 2: double, then divide by {b}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a trapezoid

formats.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides of {a} cm and {b} cm, and a height of {h} cm. What is its area?
A paper label is cut as a trapezoid with parallel sides of {a} cm and {b} cm, and a height of {h} cm. What is its area?

hints: Area of a trapezoid = (sum of the parallel sides) × height ÷ 2.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² is (sum of the parallel sides) × height. Halve it.
{value} cm² multiplies the parallel sides. Add them, then × height ÷ 2.
{value} cm² uses only the {b} cm side. Use both parallel sides: ({a} + {b}) × {h} ÷ 2.

templates.construct: Solve a problem with the area of a trapezoid

formats.prompt: A rice field is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are {a} m and {b} m long, and they are {h} m apart. What is its area?
A garden plot is a trapezoid with parallel sides of {a} m and {b} m, {h} m apart. How many square metres is it?

hints: Area of a trapezoid = (sum of the parallel sides) × height ÷ 2.

distractors.feedback: {value} m² is (sum of the parallel sides) × height. Halve it.
{value} adds lengths. Area is (sum of the parallel sides) × height ÷ 2.

templates.construct: Convert square metres to square centimetres

formats.prompt: {m} m² = ? cm²

hints: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² is a square 100 cm by 100 cm.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² uses 1 m = 100 cm. A square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm: 10000 cm².
{value} cm² uses 1000. 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10000 cm².

templates.construct: Convert square centimetres to square metres

formats.prompt: {c} cm² = ? m²

distractors.feedback: {value} m² divides by 100. A square metre is 10000 cm².
{value} m² divides by 1000. A square metre is 10000 cm².

templates.construct: Count square tiles for a floor, converting metres to centimetres

formats.prompt: A floor is {W} m by {L} m. How many square tiles, {t} cm on each side, cover it?
The floor of a sari-sari store is {W} m by {L} m. It is covered with square tiles {t} cm on each side. How many tiles are used?

hints: Work in centimetres: {W} m = {100 * W} cm and {L} m = {100 * L} cm.
{100 * W} ÷ {t} = {across} tiles across, {100 * L} ÷ {t} = {down} tiles down.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the floor in square metres. The tiles are measured in centimetres: convert first.
{value} adds the rows and columns. Multiply them: {across} × {down}.

templates.construct: Find the area of an L-shaped figure by taking a corner away

formats.prompt: An L-shaped room is made from a rectangle {W} m by {H} m, with a corner {w} m by {h} m cut away. What is the area of the room?
A garden is a rectangle {W} m by {H} m, with a corner {w} m by {h} m taken out for a shed. What is the area of the garden?

hints: Find the area of the whole rectangle, then take away the corner.

distractors.feedback: {value} m² adds the corner. It was cut away: take it off.
{value} m² is the whole rectangle. Take away the {w} m by {h} m corner.

templates.construct: Find the area of a rectangle with a triangle on top

formats.prompt: The end wall of a house is a rectangle {w} m wide and {h} m high, with a triangle on top that is {w} m wide and {t} m high. What is the area of the wall?
A billboard is a rectangle {w} m wide and {h} m high, with a triangle {t} m high on top along its whole width. What is the area of the billboard?

hints: Add the rectangle and the triangle.

distractors.feedback: {value} m² treats the triangle as a rectangle. A triangle is base × height ÷ 2.
{value} m² is only the rectangle. Add the triangle on top.

templates.construct: Find the perimeter of an L-shaped figure

formats.prompt: An L-shaped lot is made from a rectangle {W} m by {H} m, with a corner {w} m by {h} m cut away. How many metres of fence go around it?

hints: Walk around the outside and add every side.
The two sides of the notch make up for the corner: across they add to {W}, up they add to {H}.
So the perimeter is the same as the whole rectangle's: 2 × ({W} + {H}).
steps: The six sides are {W}, {H}, {W - w}, {h}, {w} and {H - h}
templates.explain: Cutting a corner leaves the perimeter the same: 2 × ({W} + {H}) = {answer} m.

distractors.feedback: {value} m adds only the four lengths given. Count every side of the L: six of them.
{value} m takes the corner's sides off. The notch's two inner sides make up for them.
{value} is the area in square metres. The fence goes around: add the sides.

templates.construct: Solve a painting problem with area

formats.prompt: A wall is {w} m long and {h} m high. One can of paint covers {c} m². How many cans are needed to paint the wall once?
Aling Nena paints one wall of her store, {w} m long and {h} m high. One can of paint covers {c} m². How many cans does she need to paint it once?

hints: First find the area of the wall.

distractors.feedback: {value} m² is the area. Divide by {c} to find the cans.
{value} uses the distance around the wall. Paint covers the area: {w} × {h}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a triangle when its slanted side is given too

formats.prompt: A triangular garden has a base of {b} m and a height of {h} m. Its slanted side is {s} m long. What is its area?

hints: The area of a triangle uses the base and the height.
The slanted side is not the height: the {s} m is not needed.
templates.explain: {b} × {h} ÷ 2 = {answer} m². The slanted side was extra information: the height is measured straight up from the base.

distractors.feedback: {fmt(value)} m² uses the slanted side. The height is the {h} m measured straight up from the base.
{value} m² is the rectangle round the triangle. A triangle is half of it.

templates.construct: Find the area of a triangle drawn on squared paper

formats.prompt: Each small square on the grid is 1 square unit. What is the area of the triangle?

hints: The triangle is half of a rectangle {b} squares wide and {h} squares tall.
That rectangle is {b} × {h} = {b * h} square units.
templates.explain: The base is {b} squares and the height {h}, so the area is {b} × {h} ÷ 2 = {answer} square units.

distractors.feedback: {value} square units is the whole rectangle round the triangle. The triangle is half of it.
{value} adds the base and the height. Area multiplies them, then halves: {b} × {h} ÷ 2.

templates.construct: Find the area of a parallelogram drawn on squared paper

formats.prompt: Each small square on the grid is 1 square unit. What is the area of the parallelogram?

hints: Cut the triangle off one slanted end and move it to the other end: the shape becomes a rectangle.
The rectangle is {b} squares long and {h} squares tall.
steps: Moving the end triangle makes a {b} by {h} rectangle
templates.explain: Moving the triangle from one end to the other makes a {b} by {h} rectangle: {answer} square units.

distractors.feedback: {value} square units uses the full width, {b + s} squares. The slanted ends make up for each other: the base is {b}.
{fmt(value)} square units halves the area, as for a triangle. A parallelogram is a whole rectangle, rearranged.

templates.construct: Find the area of a trapezoid drawn on squared paper

formats.prompt: Each small square on the grid is 1 square unit. What is the area of the trapezoid?

hints: The two parallel sides are {a} and {t} squares long, and the height is {h}.
templates.explain: The parallel sides are {a} and {t} squares and the height {h}: ({a} + {t}) × {h} ÷ 2 = {answer} square units.

distractors.feedback: {value} square units uses only the bottom side, as if it were a rectangle. Average the two parallel sides: ({a} + {t}) ÷ 2.
{value} square units is twice the area. After ({a} + {t}) × {h}, halve it.
